prompt:
A full-length figure of an enemy for the pre-fight screen of a mythology card game, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration, exactly matching the game's painted backgrounds: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour, in the limited palette given below. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting or anatomy rendering, no glossy highlights, no glow, no soft gradients, no fine fur or skin detail, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art or AI art. A strong, menacing pose facing the viewer as an opponent about to fight; the whole figure fits inside the frame. Cut out cleanly on a fully transparent background: no ground, no scenery, no frame, no text.

Subject: Polyphemus the Cyclops of Homer's Odyssey: a towering, hairy shepherd giant with a single huge glaring eye in the middle of his brow, wild black beard, a sheepskin over his shoulders, gripping a club made from a whole olive trunk, a ram at his feet, roaring. Greek in every detail.
Colour: near-black browns and deep rust (#1a0b07 to #6b2a14) with ember-orange accents.
